title: Streamlined model onboarding contracts with lifecycle webhooks
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: Onboarding new model binaries produces fragile, manually-signed performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) and ad-hoc verification notes. This results in stale profiles, unclear audit trail, and frequent manual rollbacks when runtime or hardware changes alter performance characteristics.

Goal: Deliver an automated signed-manifest contract and lifecycle webhooks for each onboarded model version. The signed manifest (SHA256) will include canonical perf signatures, sampling telemetry anchors, and reverify triggers. Webhooks will notify runtime, console, and CI systems to initiate continuous verification, canarying, and rollback when thresholds are breached.

Scope: Build manifest schema v2, signing service integration (KMS-backed), Git-backed manifest registry, lifecycle webhook spec, server-side verifier that runs sample telemetry against runtime anchors, and a console UI area for manifest history and audit logs. Provide migration tooling for existing profiles and a rollout plan with gradual adoption by the onboarding pipeline.

Out of scope: Training-time evaluation pipelines, long-term offline archival beyond the registry TTL, and embedding-only model special cases (handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema v2 defined and documented (fields: model_digest, runtime_constraints, sample_prompts, perf_signatures {p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1k_tokens}, sampling_config, signed_by, signed_at, ttl)
Signing service implemented using customer KMS for Private installs and Redwood KMS for Hosted; signatures verifiable with public key endpoint
Onboarding pipeline emits signed manifest for every model-version and stores it in Git-backed registry with immutable tag
Lifecycle webhooks implemented (events: manifest.published, manifest.reverify_required, manifest.revoked) with retry and dead-letter behavior
Server-side verifier can run sampled telemetry against runtime anchors and generate pass/fail with diff details
Console shows manifest timeline, current verification state, last-sample metrics, and a one-click rollback to last-known-good manifest
Automated canary job runs at publish time (shadow traffic <=1%) and must pass gating thresholds before manifest is promoted
Migration script converts >=90% of existing verified profiles into v2 manifests without data loss or ambiguous fields
Security review completed and key-rotation playbook documented
Monitoring/dashboards (latency drift, reverify rate, failed-promotes) created and linked to on-call runbooks
tasks: Design manifest v2 schema and backwards-compat mappings
Implement signing service and KMS integration
Extend onboarding pipeline to produce signed manifests
Build verifier microservice and define telemetry anchors
Implement webhook broker and delivery guarantees
Console UI: manifest timeline and rollback UX
Create migration tooling for legacy profiles
Create dashboards and SLO/alerting for reverify and drift
Write automation tests and end-to-end canary tests
Prepare runbook and security/key rotation docs
risks: Signing key compromise or misconfiguration could invalidate many manifests; mitigated by KMS, key rotation, and short TTLs
Runtime kernel upgrades may change perf baselines and cause churn; we will include reverify triggers tied to runtime-version metadata
Migration ambiguity from legacy profiles could create drift; include human-in-the-loop verification for edge cases
Over-zealous gating could slow model publishing cadence; adjust canary sampling rates and thresholds during rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement manifest v2 and signing; run verifier against 10 internal models (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot): wire onboarding pipeline to publish manifests for beta partners; enable webhooks and console views (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual): enable automatic canary gating for new publishes with opt-out; migrate legacy profiles with human review (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): enforce signed manifests for all verified profiles; publish playbook and train SRE/Support teams
metrics: % of new model versions published with valid signed manifest >= 95%
Mean time to detect perf drift after runtime change <= 4 hours
Rate of manual rollbacks caused by stale profiles reduced by 70%
qa_plan: Unit tests for signing and verification code paths
Integration tests between onboarding pipeline, signing service, and Git registry
E2E canary job that simulates shadow traffic and validates gating logic
Chaos test: simulated kernel update with controlled latency regression to validate rollback
Security pentest focused on key management and signature verification endpoints
